subject: SE and 95% CI in an occupancy model

messages.author: fdaa54d30ab7b913
messages.subject: SE and 95% CI in an occupancy model
parts:
Dear list members,

I got the following output from an occupancy model:

> P
  Predicted         SE        lower     upper x2
1 0.9994849 0.01699027 1.583592e-25 1.0000000  M
2 0.4911661 0.29536708 8.693091e-02 0.9072928 SM

My question is, why there is such a "contradiction" between the SE and the  95% CI?

Thank you very much in advance.

Manuel

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] SE and 95% CI in an occupancy model
parts:
Hi Manuel,

Although this appears to be a bug, I think the real problem relates to
the use of the delta method when you are near a parameter boundary.
What happens is that the SE of the beta coefficient is usually very
high when you are near a boundary, but the back-transformed SE can be
very small. As for the backtransformed CI, unmarked ensures that it is
constrained to the appropriate domain by working with the SE from the
beta estimates. That is why you see the discrepancy. The associated
code is here https://github.com/rbchan/unmarked/blob/master/R/unmarkedLinComb.R.

So, possible options are:

1. Use CI = Est +/- 1.96*SE and realize that the CI may not be
properly constrained
2. Use "nonparboot" or "parboot".
3. Become a Bayesian so that you don't have to worry about these approximations!

Option 2 is probably best if you have the time.

Richard


In this case, I would suggest using a non-parametric bootstrap
